importance_ranking.reason: Enormous visual variation across sub-types — FRP cabin vs mobile van vs tank-only, single-seat vs multi-seater community block, Indian vs Western style. Buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text; wrong sub-type is an immediate skip.

Number of seats and tank capacity are the primary shortlisting criteria — they define the scale, deployment fit, and price tier of the unit. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated by institutional buyers.

Indian institutional buyers are price-aggressive but price is only comparable after seat count, tank capacity, and material type are matched. Large municipal and railway orders are project-quoted; listed price serves as a budget entry point for initial shortlisting.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant consumer-facing brand with buyer recall; buyers search by DRDO certification, manufacturing credentials, and government supply track record — not by manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: DRDO technology certification, government/railway supply track record, and manufacturing credentials are evaluated during vendor selection for tender eligibility. Company is not a first-scan signal but is critical for institutional procurement qualification.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Single-cabin units are quoted per piece; multi-seater vans per unit/set; large institutional blocks per project or per seat. Per piece vs per project creates real price comparison confusion — unit must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit ambiguity is a genuine risk in this category — the same seller may quote per piece for a single cabin and per project for a community block. Buyers cannot compare prices without knowing the unit basis.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the scale of the unit — a 1-seat cabin and an 8-seat community block are non-interchangeable products with price deltas of several multiples, making this the primary product class separator.

Directly determines biodigester treatment capacity and drives the largest price delta within the same seat-count tier — a 500L tank vs 3000L tank represents a significant cost difference for the same cabin configuration.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Institutional buyers including Indian Railways, Defence, and municipal corporations require DRDO-certified biodigester technology as a compliance gate — uncertified units are ineligible for government tenders regardless of other specs.

Stationary cabin, mobile toilet van, and portable unit are non-interchangeable deployment types with distinct structural requirements, pricing, and buyer use cases — a construction site buyer and a municipal van buyer cannot substitute one for the other.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Indian vs Western pan configuration is non-interchangeable — rural government deployments and railway coaches typically require Indian style, while urban and institutional buyers may specify Western; sellers need this to confirm they supply the correct configuration.

FRP, MS, and GI cabins differ substantially in weight, durability, cost, and suitability for deployment context (FRP for lightweight/portable, MS for heavy-duty/permanent); sellers need this to confirm they manufacture in the required material.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Seat count defines the scale of the entire procurement — a single-seat portable unit and a 10-seat community block require completely different products, manufacturing processes, and pricing; sellers cannot respond accurately without this information.
